text: Liberalism [Lat. liber , free]: Ger. Liberalismus ; Fr. libéralisme ; Ital. liberalismo . (1) The personal disposition to free and untrammelled thought and action. (2) The social sentiment which welcomes reforming and progressive opinion and action. Liberalism is opposed to conservatism in both these meanings; but a certain relative balance between them is necessary to stable social organization, in which the writer ( Social and Eth . Interpret ., chap. v. § 3; cf. Royce, Psychol . Rev ., v. 1898, 113) has likened them to habit and accommodation in the individual's life. Extreme liberalism, taking the form of a disposition to accept innovations as such, is called radicalism. Literature : see SOCIOLOGY, and SOCIAL PSYCHOLOGY. ( J.M.B. , F.H.G. )
